speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are a newborn presenting with feeding intolerance and bilious vomiting. To determine the cause, can you tell me exactly how many days old you are and when these symptoms first started?

speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, 3050-g (6-lb 12-oz) male, six hours post delivery. The newborn has had several episodes of bilious vomiting and is intolerant to feeding since birth. Was born at term following an uncomplicated pregnancy, though the mother missed several prenatal checkups. The patient's older brother underwent surgery for pyloric stenosis as an infant.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Duodenal Atresia

The history of bilious vomiting within six hours of birth in a newborn with a male sibling who had pyloric stenosis is highly suggestive of a surgical obstruction. While pyloric stenosis is unlikely given the onset and bilious nature of the vomiting, the presence of bilious emesis in a neonate is a surgical emergency until proven otherwise.
